components.name: Hierarchy of Environmental Effects
components.description: A postulated sequence of environmental effects on health: Nontoxic ⇒ safe (physical and psychologic) ⇒ positive context ⇒ salutogenic.

components.name: Green Guidelines for Healthcare Construction (GGHC)
components.description: A quantifiable tool to guide facility planning, design, construction, and operation toward enhanced environmental and health performance, emphasizing limiting exposure to harmful chemicals and substances throughout the building process.
components.validation: Modeled after LEED™ rating system, self-certifying.

components.name: Feng Shui Principles
components.description: An ancient Chinese study of the natural environment used to determine favorable locations and promote an optimally productive and harmonious environment by balancing 'chi' or energy flow, considering elemental aspects, individuals, and solar system movements.

components.name: Anthroposophic Medicine Principles
components.description: An extension of medical practice incorporating a holistic view of the human being (material, life, soul, spirit) and its relationship with nature, influencing architecture and art.

components.name: Color Therapy Modalities
components.description: Various methods including exposure to colored lights, body work with color-saturated oils, visualizations, and eating colored foods, aimed at promoting health and affecting mood/behavior.

components.name: Sacred Geometry Principles
components.description: Belief systems focusing on building orientation and design (e.g., Sthapatya Ved, Vastu) to align with cosmic blueprints and promote health, prosperity, and spiritual growth.

components.name: Planetree Hospital Model
components.description: A patient-centered philosophy of care with ten core components, including design, focused on personalizing, humanizing, and demystifying the patient experience through access to information, family involvement, and positive human interactions.

components.name: Ulrich's Theory of Supportive Healthcare Design
components.description: An evidence-based framework for environmental design that eliminates stressful characteristics, reduces stress, calms patients, strengthens coping resources, and provides access to nature and positive distractions.

recommended_use: To inform the creation of design guidelines for the physical elements of an optimal healing environment; to make meaningful contributions to health outcomes.
limitations: Most relevant research is concentrated on a limited number of settings and is inadequate to inform the creation of design guidelines for the physical elements of an optimal healing environment.
There is inadequate research reported on the relationship of temperature to health outcomes.
The authors have not found any research on the effect on health outcomes in hospitals with operable windows.
How visible light affects mood requires more research.
Claims for the effects of ambient colors in indoor environments (e.g., pink walls calming prisoners) are largely anecdotal.
There is little or no research on sacred geometry.
A limited number of rigorous studies on health care environments exist.
Only 84 of 78,761 published studies used adequate methodologies in a review of research demonstrating a relationship between environment and health outcomes.
A broader literature review focusing on pediatric environments also found little rigorous research on the effects of environmental design on health and healing.
There is no sound, directly relevant research yet available for many health care environmental design questions.
Much of the data informing efforts to create healing environments are anecdotal or under-researched.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Exposure to non-threatening natural environments elicits rapid, pre-attentive positive affective and physiological responses that reduce stress and improve health.

mechanism_chain.description: The paper describes a causal pathway where specific environmental features, particularly natural elements, trigger rapid, pre-attentive affective and physiological responses, leading to stress reduction and improved health outcomes.

steps.from_construct: exposure to natural views or elements
steps.to_construct: elicitation of positive affect and reduced physiological arousal (e.g., lower heart rate, muscle tension)

steps.from_construct: reduced physiological arousal and positive affect

steps.to_construct: improved health outcomes (e.g., faster recovery from surgery, reduced pain perception, enhanced immune function)
